comment: Per-resort corrections applied by pipeline/normalize_osm.py (ADR-036). See whistler-blackcomb.overrides.json for the format. NO POLYGON: OpenStreetMap has no landuse=winter_sports polygon for Donner Ski Ranch (checked 2026-11-19: relation/3184079, 'Donner Ski Ranch', is a type=site, site=piste relation that lists its lifts and runs, not an area), so resorts.json sets "ski_area": "derived": the area is drawn from the resort's own kept lifts and runs, buffered by 100 m (one part, 1.54 km²; the resort says more than 500 acres). Donner Ski Ranch's front side (Chairs 1, 4 and 6 from the main lodge on Donner Pass Road) and back side (Chairs 2, 3 and 5 from the summit and the back-side lodge) are one ski area on one ticket and one map, joined at the summit by their runs; no part is reached only by road or shuttle (the trail map draws one area, front side and back side). NEIGHBOURS: no lift or trail joins Donner Ski Ranch to Sugar Bowl or to Boreal on either side's map or in OpenStreetMap, so each has its own map (the owner's rule of 2026-11-14). Sugar Bowl (relation/10326057, across Donner Pass Road; the nearest Donner Ski Ranch run, South Bowl Road, ends 250 m from its polygon) and Tahoe Donner (relation/10906075, in the Overpass window's north-east corner) are listed neighbours in resorts.json (157 and 23 features left out). Boreal (relation/3184061) and Soda Springs (relation/3185906) have only type=site relations, no polygon, so they cannot be listed, and each of their lifts and runs in the Overpass window is hidden here one by one, as Sugar Bowl's file hides Donner Ski Ranch's, Boreal's and Soda Springs': Boreal's 7 lifts and 31 runs (its Sunrise Blvd. passes 150 m from the bottom of Chair 5, the two areas' closest approach), Boreal's disused Quicksilver chair, Soda Springs' 5 lifts and 18 runs, and the two unnamed rope tows by Soda Springs Road on no resort's relation. With a derived ski area a listed neighbour leaves out only what its polygon holds at least half of, so three Sugar Bowl features outside Sugar Bowl's polygon are hidden too (the Sugar Rush tubing carpet, an unnamed run on the Crow's Peak side and the Lincoln East Face backcountry area): otherwise they would be kept and add parts to the derived area. Each hide expects the element's kind and name only, so a rating edit at a neighbour never stops this build; a polygon mapped for Boreal or Soda Springs later replaces its hides with a neighbours entry, and one mapped for Donner Ski Ranch itself replaces "derived" with its id (a new version). Nothing of Donner Ski Ranch's own is lost: every lift and run its site relation lists is kept but the tubing hill's carpet (hidden below) and its lanes (piste:type=sled, left out by the type rule). RATINGS AND NAMES: every named run and lift checked on 2026-11-19 against the resort's trail map (donnerskiranch.com/mountain-info, DonnerSkiRanch_TrailMap, the painting with its numbered run list, fetched at 2500 x 2500 px and read in crops: three grades, Easier (green), More Difficult (blue) and Most Difficult (black), the front side's runs 1 to 26 and the back side's 27 to 52) and its lift status page (donnerskiranch.com/liftstatus: Chair 1 to Chair 6, the Ski Moving Carpet and the Tubing Hill). OSM's easy and novice, intermediate and advanced match the three grades, and every named OSM run carries the map's rating but three, where the run list colours the run black and the painting's marker on the line is a blue square: the resort's own sources disagree, so the harder rating is kept (the rule of 2026-10-22) for Hut Run, Trail Blazer and Castle Peak's lower traverse (its top way is black in OSM and on the painting). Names: OSM's Chairlift 1 to Chairlift 6 become Chair 1 to Chair 6 (the lift status page; the map labels CHAIR #1 to CHAIR #6), and the unnamed ski carpet by Chair 4 takes the map's MOVING CARPET. Names that differ from the map only by a space, a hyphen or an apostrophe stay as OSM has them (Easy Rider for EASYRIDER, Crossover for CROSS OVER, Cross Under for CROSSUNDER, Lake View for LAKEVIEW, Springboard for SPRING BOARD, Sidewinder for SIDE WINDER, Mertyl's Cut-off for MERTYL'S CUTOFF), and so does Sanctuary, which the run list misspells SANTUARY. Half Pipe (33) is a black run on the map, not a terrain park, and the map draws no park. OSM's Lance's Leap (advanced) is not on the map and stays as OSM has it. OSM GAPS (shipped as at Palisades Tahoe): 7 of the map's 52 runs are not in OpenStreetMap: Palisades (black), Sand Pit Road and Not So Private Road (green), Snow Catch (blue in the run list, a green circle on the painting), Lift Off (black), Cat Tracks and Boomerang (blue).

Hut Run is listed in black (most difficult) in the trail map's run list (36. Hut Run) while the painting marks its line with a blue square and OSM rates it intermediate: the resort's own sources disagree, so the harder rating is kept (the rule of 2026-10-22).

Trail Blazer is listed in black (most difficult) in the trail map's run list (40. Trail Blazer) while the painting marks its line with a blue square and OSM rates it intermediate: the resort's own sources disagree, so the harder rating is kept (the rule of 2026-10-22).

Castle Peak's lower way, the traverse west to the bottom of Chair 3 (482 m), which OSM rates intermediate (its 117 m top way, way/879912942, is advanced): the trail map's run list gives Castle Peak in black (most difficult, 38. Castle Peak), while the painting marks the run's top with a black diamond and this traverse with a blue square. The resort's own sources disagree on this way, so the harder rating is kept (the rule of 2026-10-22), as for Hut Run and Trail Blazer.
